id: title:jakesciotto:don t remount on repeat ph load toolbar calls

review.posthog_relevance: These changes address DOM stability and state consistency for the PostHog toolbar widget, preventing duplicate mounts and race conditions during Single Page Application (SPA) route changes. This supports the reliability of the embedded analytics experience.
review.reason: The observed changes implement shared in-flight promises and mounted-state guards to prevent duplicate toolbar mounting and DOM stacking, and distinguish between loaded and detached states. This represents a substantive, bounded improvement in the reliability and correctness of the PostHog frontend widget behavior.
review.uncertainty: The tier is assigned based on the implementation of state guards and deduplication, which warrants a score of 2. However, the actual runtime benefit and complete absence of edge-case failures are not independently verified by this code review, and the broader impact on PostHog's ecosystem is inferred rather than demonstrated.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains only test and implementation changes. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds idempotency and deduplication guards to toolbar loading.
observations.posthog_connection: Prevents duplicate toolbar mounts and DOM stacking when posthog-js re-invokes ph_load_toolbar on SPA route changes.

observations.behavior: Adds a shared in-flight promise and mounted-state guard.
observations.posthog_connection: Deduces overlapping concurrent calls to avoid mounting a second toolbar while the first is still initializing.

observations.behavior: Adds a mounted-state check combining loaded flag and DOM attachment.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the toolbar to distinguish between a loaded-but-detached state and a healthy mounted state, enabling recovery remounts when the host page removes the container.
